verbalization: Cytidine exerts its biological effects through interaction with UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2A1, an enzyme involved in drug metabolism and detoxification. This enzyme is a target of the antibiotic Cespitulactam K, which is known to inhibit the activity of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2A1. The inhibition of this enzyme by Cespitulactam K leads to the accumulation of cytotoxic substrates, which in turn can induce cellular stress and ultimately contribute to the death of cancer cells, as observed in the model system HCC1937. The observed relationship between Cytidine and HCC1937 is thus mediated through a cascade involving UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2A1 and Cespitulactam K, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy that targets this metabolic pathway to modulate the behavior of HCC1937 cells.
